transcript:
Header:
Date: 2029-05-06
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Ellen Brooks (Redwood Product), Samir Rao (Cedarwood Head of Platform), Linda Gomez (Privacy Officer), Tom Vale (SRE), Priya Nair (Product)

AutoSummary: Quick demo of console + API flow for ephemeral request storage (TTL), routing sensitive fields to private deployment, and how to use per-route overrides; customer asked about KMS, SOC2, and pilot sizing.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maria Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for making time — Maria from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Samir Rao: Samir here, hi.
[00:09] Linda Gomez: Linda.
[00:11] Tom Vale: Tom.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Priya.
[00:14] Maria Chen: Great, quick agenda — demo the request storage toggles in Console, show how we route based on detected sensitive fields, and run through a short pilot proposal. Ravi will jump in for the technical bits. Any additions?
[00:25] Samir Rao: No, that's good. We're really focused on making sure anything with SSNs or PII doesn't leave our VPC or gets purged quickly. Latency matters for tracking, but cost also matters.
[00:40] Ravi Patel: Totally. I'll demonstrate three pieces: per-route TTL, ephemeral logs, and a sensitive-field routing rule that can route a request to a private deployment when certain fields are detected.
[00:51] Ellen Brooks: I'll show the Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization after the demo.
[00:56] Maria Chen: Ok, starting console share — apologies if transcription of the paste is messy, I'll narrate.
[01:07] Maria Chen: Here is the Request Storage policy page — we have global defaults for retention, and per-route overrides. Example: 30 days global, but you can set a route to ephemeral with TTL of 30 seconds or 24 hours.
[01:22] Tom Vale: Can TTL be sub-minute? We have debug traces that we want ephemeral for a few minutes only.
[01:28] Ravi Patel: Yes, sub-minute TTLs are allowed, down to 10 seconds. There is a caveat around streaming responses — we'll explain.
[01:36] Linda Gomez: How is PII detected? We have custom classes — SSN is obvious but we also have government IDs and internal account numbers.
[01:44] Ravi Patel: The console uses a combination of regex rules and ML classifiers; you can upload custom rules. For pilot we'd recommend starting with custom rule list from Linda plus Redwood's classifier. If a rule matches, you can do two things: redact in-place and keep logs ephemeral, or route the whole request to your Private deployment (VPC) and never persist on hosted logs.
[02:03] Priya Nair: Route to Private — that implies extra cost & latency. We need to understand tradeoffs.
[02:09] Maria Chen: Right, we surface that in the UI — per-route cost delta and estimated latency impact. For private routing we can do header-based routing or content-based routing; content-based will add about ~10-30ms depending on model size and kernel path.
[02:25] Samir Rao: Are we able to redaction at the SDK level so logs never even get to the edge?
[02:31] Ravi Patel: Yes, we have client-side SDK flags you can enable to do pre-scrub; it's best-effort for performance. For strict compliance we recommend a combination: client-side redaction + server-side detection + route to Private for full isolation.
[02:46] Tom Vale: KMS? Audit trail? We need proofs for auditors.
[02:49] Ellen Brooks: We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations and provide immutable audit logs for all routing decisions; those logs can be exported to your SIEM.
[02:59] Linda Gomez: Can we disable request storage entirely for certain routes? For instance, any route that touches healthcare PII should never be stored.
[03:06] Ravi Patel: Yes — set retention to ephemeral and enable "never persist" flag; that ensures no token-level storage and strips metadata beyond routing, and we mark that in the audit log. Note: when you set "never persist" you cannot use quality regressions tooling for that route since we don't keep content.
[03:23] Maria Chen: Demoing per-route rule creation now — adding a condition: if field.name matches regex for SSN or label is PII with severity high, then action = route_to_private(west-eu-vpc) + retention=ephemeral(10s).
[03:40] Maria Chen: Uploading a custom rule file — you can also test on sample payloads in the console.
[03:46] Priya Nair: Nice. Can we fallback if private capacity is exhausted?
[03:50] Ravi Patel: Yes, you can configure policy: fail-open (deny request), fallback to hosted with redaction, or queue/buffer until capacity is available. Default recommended is fallback to hosted redaction with an alert; for strict compliance choose fail-open deny.
[04:06] Samir Rao: For SRE, how do we monitor routing? Is there per-route telemetry?
[04:10] Ellen Brooks: Per-route telemetry includes counts routed to private, queued, denied, and latency percentiles. You can drill into per-tenant traces but content is only visible if retention > ephemeral.
[04:22] Tom Vale: About encryption at rest — if something is persisted briefly, is it encrypted with our CMK?
[04:26] Ravi Patel: Yes, any persisted token-level data can be encrypted with your CMK via our KMS integration. Ephemeral storage also uses envelope encryption, but keys rotate frequently and you control rotation.
[04:36] Linda Gomez: Are deletion requests (GDPR right to be forgotten) honored for hosted logs? Do you provide receipts?
[04:42] Maria Chen: We expose a deletion API and a deletion job with a verifiable receipt; for private deployments you control deletion within your environment. We can include the deletion receipts in the audit export.
[04:55] Priya Nair: Can the routing make decisions on vector embeddings or is it only plaintext fields?
[04:59] Ravi Patel: Currently content-based routing runs on request payloads pre-embedding. We are working on metadata and embedding-based signals as a roadmap item.
[05:08] Maria Chen: Switching to API examples — here's a snippet for setting per-route TTL via config-as-code: route.policy.retention.ttl_seconds = 30; route.policy.action.on_pii = "route_private:us-east-1". You can push via API or set in the console.
[05:26] Samir Rao: Great. About streaming earlier — you mentioned a caveat?
[05:30] Ravi Patel: Streaming responses require a short-lived hold to maintain the KV cache on the runtime; ephemeral TTLs shorter than the stream duration will cause truncation for long-running streams. So pick TTLs > expected stream time.
[05:44] Tom Vale: For our tracers we sometimes ingest full transcripts — can we redact post-hoc?
[05:47] Ravi Patel: We provide redaction jobs that run post ingestion, but redaction is best done pre-ingestion; post-hoc redaction is possible but might leave ephemeral indexes in traces until the job runs. We can prioritize redaction jobs in pilot.
[06:02] Priya Nair: Let's talk pilot sizing — we want to mirror peak daily traffic which is around 450 rps for the customer-facing tracking route and 120 rps for internal backoffice.
[06:12] Ravi Patel: For pilot we'll recommend running a 2-week pilot that includes a dedicated small pool (reserved burst) for private routing. We'll set sample traffic to 500 rps to be safe and run profiling across 90th/99th percentiles.
[06:25] Samir Rao: How do we measure cost impact? We need to show delta if 10% of requests route private, and 3% require never-persist.
[06:32] Ellen Brooks: The console shows per-route cost breakdown: model compute + routing delta + storage. We'll export a delta report estimate for the scenarios you gave.
[06:41] Maria Chen: Quick interjection — competitors? Anyone we need to call out?
[06:44] Samir Rao: We've looked at Anthropic and some in-house attempts. Anthropic has certain compliance features but their routing is less fine-grained.
[06:54] Linda Gomez: Also we evaluated OpenAI for simple use cases but we need private routing and tight TTLs.
[06:59] Maria Chen: Good color. Ellen, can you run the Optimize suggestions?
[07:02] Ellen Brooks: Sure — showing Optimize tab. For your tracking route, suggestions: reduce seq length, enable prefix KV caching for repeated context, and a lightweight quantization profile for non-sensitive requests. For sensitive routes we recommend no quantization and dedicated CPU-GPU mapping to ensure determinism.
[07:21] Priya Nair: So Optimize can recommend different profiles by route?
[07:23] Ellen Brooks: Exactly — per-route optimization profiles that factor cost, latency, and quality. You can pin profiles per-deployment.
[07:31] Tom Vale: Any SDK changes for client-side redaction? Which languages?
[07:35] Ravi Patel: We have SDK flags in JS, Python, and Java. We also provide a middleware that intercepts fields and applies your custom rule set; it's open-source on GitHub.
[07:45] Samir Rao: About audit logs — can we push them to our Splunk?
[07:48] Ellen Brooks: Yes, direct export via webhook or S3 export; we also have a Splunk connector.
[07:55] Linda Gomez: A note on legal — our procurement wants clear terms about PII handling; can you share privacy bindings?
[07:59] Maria Chen: We'll include the privacy addendum in the follow up.
[08:02] Priya Nair: One more: what happens if our custom regex false-positive rates are high? We can't route everything to private.
[08:08] Ravi Patel: Console gives you false-positive metrics if you run a dry-run mode — it reports matches and confidence. You can tune classifier thresholds and run rule fine-tuning before enabling route enforcement. Dry-run is highly recommended.
[08:22] Samir Rao: For SLAs — what's the latency SLA for hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[08:27] Ellen Brooks: Hosted API: best effort with SLOs surfaced; Dedicated has SLA-backed p50/p95; private depends on your infra, but Redwood provides guidance and an optional management agent for on-prem performance monitoring. We'll attach SLA doc.
[08:40] Maria Chen: Wrapping up — recap and next steps. We'll send SOC2/KMS docs, a sample routing + TTL config, a pilot plan, and a pricing delta estimate. Any blockers?
[08:51] Linda Gomez: None that I see; Linda will finalize PII field list.
[08:55] Samir Rao: I'll send traffic profile.
[08:57] Maria Chen: Great — we'll target the pilot kick on 2029-05-20 pending paperwork. Thanks all.
[09:05] (end of recording)

Notes on transcription accuracy: occasional mislabeling and dropped punctuation in code snippets. Certain proprietary names may be rendered roughly (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes as "K V cache").
